properties.name: The loop can answer what this design owes a NAMED PERSON, not only what it owes in total
properties.statement:
Raised by @ajs from flo2, 2026-08-05. It began as friction — a proposed Decision that nothing reported — and became the largest open question in flo2's design when it was put as a product question instead: "Shawn proposes an idea in flo2. How does that ever surface to Alex or me?" Today it does not. Not reliably, and not at all without someone independently deciding to go and look.

TRACE IT THROUGH, because three links are missing and the chain needs all three. (1) IS IT VISIBLE TO THE LOOP? Sometimes. A proposed Requirement with nothing satisfying it does fire unsatisfied_requirement, so that case works. A proposed Decision fires nothing. So whether a contribution is visible depends on which node type it happened to be captured as — an implementation detail the contributor cannot see and should not have to care about. (2) DOES ANYTHING SAY WHOSE IT IS? No. The gap says a requirement is unsatisfied; nothing says Shawn raised this, or that @ajs should judge it. AUTHORED_BY with role=approver already exists and is exactly the right shape, but NOTHING COMPUTES ON IT. (3) IS ANYONE TOLD? No — and this one is structural rather than missing: proxy.rs states that the reflow2 server NEVER INITIATES A MESSAGE (no notifications, no sampling requests, no progress pushes, "verified against the service, not assumed"). Every byte belongs to a request the client started.

THE MISMATCH UNDERNEATH. reflow2's coherence loop assumes ONE PERSON AT A KEYBOARD, with an agent asking them questions in a conversation. That assumption is sound and it is why the loop works so well in a coding harness. flo2 puts people in different places at different times, so the same loop has to become asynchronous — an inbox rather than a conversation. Nothing about the graph prevents that; the loop simply has no notion of a person to owe something to.

THE CHEAP PRIMITIVE, and the reason this is a sibling rather than a new idea: loop_status today answers "what does this design owe?" and TAKES NO ARGUMENTS AT ALL, while detect_gaps already accepts a scope for "one part of the design". A contributor scope on loop_status follows an established pattern. With that, the rest is flo2's own work and is ordinary: poll per user, render the inbox, email when it grows.

NOTIFICATION IS DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE. The server never initiating a message is a property worth keeping, and flo2 can poll. What has to live in reflow2 is the ANSWER to "what is owed to this person", because only the graph knows.

THE REAL DESIGN QUESTION INSIDE THIS, not to be papered over: what "owed to" MEANS per item type. A gap on a requirement Shawn raised is arguably owed to whoever must judge it, not to him. That is a genuine question and not a small one.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE AND NOT ONLY TO flo2: this is the axis on which the accepted req:no-idea-goes-quiet currently fails. That requirement promises an idea "stays connected to whether it was built... the user never has to remember it exists" — and it holds for one person at one keyboard while failing completely for a contributor who is somewhere else.
